notes: Broadleaf shrubs and bushes — the frame's dark anchor, LIFTED OUT OF BLACK. Measured, shrub-broadleaf was rendering #202E3B at luma 0.172 and bush-round at 0.230 against reference foliage of 0.403-0.685, and on the contact sheets they read as burnt charcoal rocks rather than as vegetation. The anchor is allowed to be the darkest thing in the frame; it is not allowed to be a hole, and it is not allowed to be blue-grey (the old shadow stop measured hue 209). WHY THIS DEF EXISTS RATHER THAN AN EDIT TO `rock`/`mountain`/`foliage`/`bush`. src/world/surfaceGrade.ts applies `graded(surfaceId, params)` at the point of use, and `graded` is `{...params, ...CLEAN, ...GRADE[surfaceId]}` — so for the four ids it has an entry for, the GRADE table wins over BOTH the def and the per-def `material` override. Authoring a corrected value on `rock` therefore changed the Forge and left the game pixel exactly where it was, which is how the last round shipped a rock whose authored shadow (luma 0.51) arrived on screen at #232E66 (luma 0.187) against the reference's darkest rock facet at 0.404. These are the scatter library's OWN surface ids, so only `CLEAN` applies to them — which is what we want anyway — and the measured grade below reaches the pixel in both the Forge and the game. The old ids stay for the terrain, which is the world team's to grade. `topGain` and `gradientStrength` carry the INTRA-FACET variation. With the brush overlay gone a plane-cut facet measured luma sd 0.000-0.005 over a 60x60 window against 0.0155-0.0371 for a rock facet in the reference — flatter than the target by an order of magnitude, which reads as plastic and trips a dead-flat-tile check. The variation the reference has is a smooth vertical ramp following the FORM (ART_BIBLE 3: the vertical gradient 'is doing enormous work'), not noise, so it comes from the up-axis sweep rather than from a stroke field. `shadowSkyTint` pulled back to ~0.1. This is what was actually making the rock a NAVY CUBE, not the authored hex: the param replaces the shadow albedo with the live sky HUE at the shadow's own luminance and then runs it through `boostSaturation`, so an authored blue-grey at S0.16 arrived on screen at S0.64 hue 222 and lost most of its value doing it — measured #2B4278 luma 0.255 at noon from an authored #82919B at luma 0.58. ART_BIBLE 2 wants the shade COOLED, not recoloured, and the reference's own darkest rock facet is #397097 at luma 0.404. A small tint plus a high ambient gets both; a large tint gets neither. Value set AGAINST the meadow rather than in absolute terms: at ambient 2.2 the body measured luma 0.494 against ground 0.518-0.527, i.e. the anchor had become the same value as the thing it is supposed to anchor. 1.7 puts it near 0.40 — the low end of the reference's foliage band and about 0.8x the ground, which is a dark mass that is still unmistakably a plant.
